sentences.text: One summer day in 1518, a woman in Strasbourg walked out of her house and started dancing in the street.
Just one woman, dancing for days, while her neighbours stared.
Within weeks, dozens of people were dancing in the streets, drenched in sweat, unable to stop.
So what did the town council do?
They decided the cure was more dancing.
According to the chronicles, they cleared halls, hired musicians, and even paid strong men to keep the dancers on their feet.
Unluckily, it only made things worse.
The council banned public dancing, and the dancers were sent to a shrine to pray.
You see, historians still argue about why it happened.
The most popular idea is that fear, hunger and disease pushed people past their limits, and the panic spread from person to person, like a yawn across a crowded room.
By September, the dancing faded away, and nobody knows exactly how many danced.
But the town that tried to cure dancing with more dancing never forgot it.
